tldr: NewTokenBuffer's backward walk to the last non-blank token runs once per nested style switch over the same trailing comment run, so a cell ending in k comment lines under 255 switches costs 255k steps
details: Each switch cuts its cell with GetNextN(b.cellEnd() - b.idx), which goes through sub to NewTokenBuffer, and the loop at tokenize.go:314 walks the cell's trailing blanks from the end again. The counter reads walks equal to k times the number of switches, and zero when a token follows the run. maxSwitchDepth caps the factor at 255, so the cost stays linear in the input and below the merge base: a page of 128 such 8 KiB blocks takes 173 ms at head, 59 ms without the switches and 811 ms at the base. The body's 'every run is walked once' does not hold for this run. Deriving a sub-buffer's last from a table shared across the formula, as cellEnds is, would remove the factor; that fix was not built or run here.
